description: The plot illustrates the training loss over time for two models: “Vanilla” and “SepLLM,” as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis represents “Training Time (s)” on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis shows “Loss,” also on a linear scale, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks every 0.05 units. The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with triangular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.75 loss at 0 seconds and gradually decreases to about 2.50 loss near 250,000 seconds. The “SepLLM” model is shown with a red line and circular markers, also solid; it starts at approximately 2.72 loss and declines more steeply, reaching around 2.50 loss at approximately 200,000 seconds — marked by a green dashed box and annotation indicating “1.26×” speedup relative to Vanilla at that point. Both lines converge near 2.50 loss by 250,000 seconds, with SepLLM achieving that level significantly faster. A horizontal green dashed line at loss = 2.50 visually anchors the convergence point.
